items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: So finally, Cal Liston say, "Put that gun away,"

ctx.x: So they did that to me for two or three days. And I told them, "Now," you know what I mean, "Let's cool it." But what they would always do, Dan, and I guess this is typical of any

person that..where there are two or three people can speak a different language from one person, they'll speak in that language and say something and even if they're not talking about the person, he will think they're talking about him. They used to speak this patois, so coming back from Mineral Wells or wherever it was--we were in this big Cadillac, we had all the instruments and all this business--and they kept talking that patois and I was in the back and I came out with a gun and fired and you're talking…

But we got in Chicago and I went around every morning to the breakfast dance. You see, they had a breakfast dance. This is a thing they had every morning. They used to have those here. They called it a breakfast dance, it's just where they had a special show...say at four o'clock, the place closed at four or five o'clock. They'd have music and a dance
